bib.title: Interleaving Retrieval with Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Knowledge-Intensive Multi-Step Questions

read.skipped: References skimmed; CoT demonstration listings 1-4 read but not recorded verbatim (in released code).

question: How can retrieval be combined with chain-of-thought reasoning so that few-shot LLMs answer knowledge-intensive multi-step questions better than with one-step question-based retrieval?
hypothesis: Retrieval and reasoning must inform each other: what to retrieve depends on what has been derived, so one-step retrieval from the question alone is insufficient.
contributions: IRCoT, a retrieval method that interleaves CoT generation with retrieval, using the last CoT sentence as the query
Improves retrieval and few-shot QA on four multi-step open-domain datasets, in-distribution and out-of-distribution
Reduces factual errors in generated CoTs
Works with small models (Flan-T5, <=11B) without any training

method.summary: IRCoT retrieves K paragraphs with the question using BM25, then alternates a reason step (an LLM generates the next CoT sentence given the question, collected paragraphs and prior CoT sentences) and a retrieve step (the last CoT sentence is the BM25 query, adding K paragraphs), until 'answer is' appears or 8 steps. All collected paragraphs (max 15) go to a separate reader (Direct for Flan-T5, CoT for GPT3). Nothing is trained; few-shot prompting only.
method.task: open-domain multi-hop QA (retrieval and few-shot reading)

datasets.name: HotpotQA
datasets.size: 500 test questions + 100 dev-tuning questions, sampled from dev set; corpus 5,233,329 paragraphs
datasets.source: Wikipedia corpus that comes with HotpotQA; CC BY-SA 4.0

datasets.name: 2WikiMultihopQA
datasets.source: corpus built from all supporting and non-supporting paragraphs of train/dev/test questions; Apache-2.0

datasets.name: MuSiQue (answerable subset)
datasets.source: corpus built like 2Wiki, 20 paragraphs per question; CC BY 4.0

datasets.name: IIRC (answerable subset)
datasets.source: all paragraphs from all Wikipedia pages in the dataset; CC BY 4.0
datasets.preprocessing: paragraphs shuffled before indexing to remove positional bias; main passage always supplied; model first generates N=3 Wikipedia titles at test time, mapped to nearest corpus titles with BM25, and queries are scoped to those pages

models.name: Flan-T5-XXL / XL / large / base
models.init_from: public Flan-T5 weights, no further training

inference.decoding: For each reason step only the first generated sentence is kept, the rest discarded; decoding method not stated
inference.samples: 3 demonstration sets (15 questions each sampled from 20 hand-written CoTs per dataset); mean and std of 3 results; hyperparameters chosen with the first set on dev
inference.prompting: Few-shot; as many demonstrations as fit in context. Demonstration format: Wikipedia Title/paragraph blocks (gold paragraphs plus M distractors, shuffled), then 'Q:' and 'A:' with CoT. Flan-T5 prompts prefix 'Q: Answer the following question by reasoning step-by-step.' (CoT) or 'Q: Answer the following question.' (Direct).
inference.retrieval: BM25 via Elasticsearch; IRCoT K in {2,4,6,8} paragraphs per step; OneR K in {5,7,9,11,13,15}; total capped at 15; max 8 reasoning steps; M distractors in {1,2,3}

parameters.M: {1,2,3}, tied between CoT generator and reader
parameters.termination: 'answer is' in generated sentence or max steps

other.reader: separate reader; Direct prompting for Flan-T5, CoT prompting for GPT3
other.cost: one LLM call per CoT sentence; no latency or token cost measured

metrics.name: Retrieval recall (fixed-budget optimal recall)
metrics.definition: recall of gold paragraphs among retrieved set, max 15 paragraphs; K (and M) chosen to maximise dev recall; retrieved sets unranked so Recall@k, MAP, DCG not applicable

metrics.name: Answer F1
metrics.definition: token F1 of predicted answer; also EM in Table 1

metrics.name: Factual errors in CoT
metrics.definition: manual annotation: CoT has an error if at least one fact (all sentences before the 'answer is' sentence) is untrue

eval.protocol: 500 test questions per dataset; 3 demonstration sets, mean+-std; OOD: demonstrations from one dataset evaluated on another (IIRC skipped); factuality on 40 random questions per dataset with GPT3, manual annotation (annotator count not stated)

availability.data: prompts and data in the code repository

evidence.quote: We cap the total number of collected paragraphs5 so as to fit in at least a few demonstrations in the model’s context limit.
evidence.where: Sec 3.1 footnotes 4,5: max steps 8, max paragraphs 15

results.claim: IRCoT raises gold-paragraph recall over OneR with GPT3 on HotpotQA, 2Wiki, MuSiQue, IIRC
results.setup: GPT3 code-davinci-002; BM25 (Elasticsearch), 500 test questions per dataset sampled from dev, K and M tuned on 100 other dev questions, mean of 3 demonstration sets, retrieval capped at 15 paragraphs
results.quote: For GPT3, this improvement is by 11.3, 22.6, 12.5, and 21.2 points, respectively.

results.claim: IRCoT raises recall over OneR with Flan-T5-XXL
results.setup: Flan-T5-XXL; BM25 (Elasticsearch), 500 test questions per dataset sampled from dev, K and M tuned on 100 other dev questions, mean of 3 demonstration sets, retrieval capped at 15 paragraphs
results.quote: on HotpotQA by 7.9, on 2WikiMultihopQA by 14.3, on MuSiQue by 3.5, and on IIRC by 10.2 points

results.claim: IRCoT QA beats OneR QA with Flan-T5-XXL in answer F1
results.setup: Flan-T5-XXL, Direct reader; BM25 (Elasticsearch), 500 test questions per dataset sampled from dev, K and M tuned on 100 other dev questions, mean of 3 demonstration sets, retrieval capped at 15 paragraphs
results.quote: IRCoT QA outperforms OneR QA on HotpotQA by 9.4, on 2WikiMultihopQA by 15.3, on MuSiQue by 5.0 and IIRC by 2.5 F1 points.

results.claim: With GPT3 IRCoT QA beats OneR QA by 7.1, 13.2, 7.1 F1 on HotpotQA, 2Wiki, MuSiQue; no gain on IIRC despite ~21 recall points
results.setup: GPT3, CoT reader; BM25 (Elasticsearch), 500 test questions per dataset sampled from dev, K and M tuned on 100 other dev questions, mean of 3 demonstration sets, retrieval capped at 15 paragraphs
results.quote: the corresponding numbers (except for IIRC) are 7.1, 13.2, and 7.1 F1 points
results.note: Authors suggest IIRC knowledge is already in GPT3 (NoR score similar).

results.claim: IRCoT reduces factual errors in CoT over OneR by 50% on HotpotQA and 40% on 2Wiki
results.setup: GPT3, 40 random questions per dataset, manual annotation
results.quote: IRCoT reduces the factual errors over OneR by 50% on HotpotQA and 40% on 2WikiMultihopQA.

results.claim: IRCoT QA with 3B Flan-T5-XL beats OneR QA with 58X larger GPT3
results.setup: Flan-T5-XL (3B) IRCoT vs GPT3 175B OneR, all datasets in Fig 9
results.quote: IRCoT with a 3B model even outperforms OneR and NoR with a 58X larger 175B GPT3 model in all datasets.

results.claim: IRCoT QA with GPT3 reaches 45.8/58.5 EM/F1 on HotpotQA bridge, 49.3/60.7 on HotpotQA, 57.7/68.0 on 2Wiki, 34.2/43.8 on MuSiQue 2-hop; not head-to-head with other systems

results.note: Not head-to-head: different corpora, LLMs, subsets.

limits: Needs an LM with few-shot CoT ability, uncommon under 20B parameters
Needs long input to hold retrieved paragraphs plus demonstrations
Extra computational cost: a separate LLM call per CoT sentence; cost not measured
code-davinci-002 was deprecated, so GPT3 results are hard to reproduce; trends are believed to hold
Comparisons with other systems are not head-to-head
Retrieved sets are unranked, so standard IR metrics are not reported
Only BM25 as base retriever; Wikipedia-derived multi-hop corpora; 500 test questions per dataset
Smallest model (0.2B) QA does not improve over OneR

terms.definition: recall of gold paragraphs within a maximum of 15 retrieved paragraphs, with K (and M) chosen to maximise dev recall
